points.text: States each pH step is ten times stronger, so two steps multiply the acidity by ten then ten again
Applies the ladder the right way round, with the lower pH counted as the more acidic solution

items.prompt: One solution has pH 2 and another has pH 4. Explain which solution is more acidic and how many times more acidic it is.

points.text: Gives blue litmus turning red for the acid test
Gives red litmus turning blue for the alkali test, with no change read as neutral

items.prompt: State the colour change of litmus paper in an acid and in an alkali.

points.text: Pairs the H+ ions from the acid with the OH- ions from the alkali to form water
Accounts for the leftover ions as the salt rather than saying the two liquids cancel into nothing

items.prompt: Explain, in terms of ions, what happens when hydrochloric acid is neutralised by sodium hydroxide, and name the salt formed.

points.text: Names the nucleus as the structure controlling the cell
Names the membrane as selectively permeable, choosing what crosses rather than sealing the cell

items.prompt: Describe the job of the nucleus and of the cell membrane in an animal cell.

levels.descriptor: Explanations chain ion behaviour to the pH change in order, with each step justified by a named ion or indicator change.
levels.label: Secure

levels.descriptor: Explanations are broadly sound but one link between the ions and the pH change is asserted rather than justified.
levels.label: Developing

levels.descriptor: Answers list facts about acids and cells without connecting them into an explanation.
levels.label: Beginning
